DDInter843.mechanism: Coadministration with inducers of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) or CYP450 3A4 may decrease the plasma concentrations of glecaprevir and pibrentasvir.  Both antiviral agents are substrates of the P-gp efflux transporter, and glecaprevir is additionally a substrate of the CYP450 3A4 isoenzyme.

DDInter904.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) may increase the plasma concentrations of daunorubicin and idarubicin, both of which are substrates of the efflux transporter also known as ABCB1 or MDR1.

DDInter905.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 and/or P-glycoprotein (P-gp) may increase the plasma concentrations of idelalisib, which is a substrate of both the isoenzyme and efflux transporter.

DDInter915.mechanism: Coadministration with inhibitors of CYP450 3A4 and/or P-glycoprotein may increase the systemic exposure to indacaterol following oral inhalation, as it is a substrate of both the isoenzyme and efflux transporter.

DDInter995.mechanism: Coadministration with itraconazole may increase the plasma concentrations and risk of adverse effects of glecaprevir-pibrentasvir.  The mechanism has not been clearly established, but may involve itraconazole-mediated inhibition of P-glycoprotein (P-gp), breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP), and/or CYP450 3A4 isoenzyme.
